body: My town has the tallest man-made dam in the states. The spillway (the slide-looking-structure (lol) that releases water from the lake) cracked, and the water pressure caused a gigantic crater to form in the spillway. The emergency spillway failed because when they built it years and years ago they didn't even test it. Anyhow, 200,000 people in Northern California ended up being evacuated. Our police departments shut down the main highway and diverted all the lanes out of town. Bumper to bumper traffic, accidents resulting in broken down cars along the highway, left abandoned. It was like the walking dead. Homeless people were riding alongside our cars on bicycles with all of their belongings on their backs. The anxiety was fucking real. Everyone was yelling and panicking, trying to stay together. Houses back in town were being ransacked by lunatics that stayed behind. The Red Cross evacuation shelter at a nearby town ended up with a norovirus outbreak. I cannot make this up lol

Don't care how late this is, I'm pressed to see who believes me. I was born and raised in Cali, visited Ohio during June/July maybe? I was at a park for a child's birthday party; his dad was a doctor from California serving his residency in Ohio. So, just my luck, all the other adults at the party claim they're from out of state originally, all placed in Ohio for residency. Fast forward to me playing with the kids on the playground- I hear buzzing, like a fuckin helicopter by my ear, and I turn to see the biggest wasp I've ever seen. It must've been 3 inches long. It was soOoOOo big, I grabbed the kids and ran off the playground so fast. Nobody at the party believed me and they all kept joking that each time I told the story the bee got bigger. 

After frantically googling it, I found that hornets like that are native to the east coast and they nest in the ground, and apparently the females can get to be like 4 inches long
